web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside AbbVie's Five Franchises — Products, Patients, and Payer Economics
question: What exact medicines and aesthetic products generate AbbVie's $61.2B revenue base, and how does each therapeutic franchise work in real-world clinical practice?

epigraph.quote: AbbVie operates as one global business segment, while commercial activity is organized by therapeutic area and geography.
epigraph.author: AbbVie Inc., FY2025 Form 10-K

web_blocks.title: Portfolio Architecture: One Accounting Segment, Five Commercial Pillars

web_blocks.html: Under GAAP rules in its FY2025 Form 10-K, AbbVie reports one global pharmaceutical segment [1]. Manufacturing plants, R&D labs, and commercial teams are shared across regions [1]. In practice, management runs the business across five commercial portfolios: Immunology, Neuroscience, Oncology, Aesthetics, and Eye Care [2, 3]. It also tracks a legacy Other Key Products group that includes Creon, Mavyret, and Linzess [2, 3]. In FY2025, AbbVie posted $61,160M in global net sales [2]. The United States supplied 76.2% of total sales, or $46,603M [2]. International markets added the remaining 23.8%, or $14,557M [2]. Through Q3 2026, nine-month net sales reached $49,396M, up 10.9% year over year [3]. Immunology led the company at 51.1% of 9M 2026 sales, followed by Neuroscience at 19.2% [3].

web_blocks.caption: AbbVie Revenue Mix by Therapeutic Portfolio & Flagship Products (FY2025 & 9M 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Immunology and Neuroscience together generate 67.3% of FY2025 revenue and 70.3% of 9M 2026 revenue, carrying the entire company past Imbruvica's IRA decline and Aesthetics' dermal filler softness [2, 3, 7].

web_blocks.title: Immunology ($30.4B in FY25): Concrete Patient-to-Payer Walkthrough

web_blocks.html: Immunology is AbbVie's crown jewel. Skyrizi (an IL-23p19 antibody) and Rinvoq (an oral JAK1 inhibitor) lead the franchise, while legacy Humira tapers down [2, 3]. AbbVie does not disclose operating profit by therapeutic area. Instead, we infer high margins from its 83.6%–85.1% adjusted gross margin, which leans heavily toward U.S. specialty immunology [2, 3]. Consider a real-world example in Crohn's disease. A 34-year-old patient with moderate-to-severe ileocolonic Crohn's visits a community gastroenterologist after failing steroids and an anti-TNF biologic. The doctor prescribes Skyrizi. In the past, the patient needed three intravenous induction infusions at a clinic before starting an at-home on-body injector every eight weeks. Following FDA approval of Skyrizi subcutaneous induction in late 2026, the patient can now start therapy at home with the same on-body injector [3, 7]. AbbVie ships the drug via a specialty pharmacy like CVS Specialty or Accredo. The pharmacy verifies prior authorization with the patient's commercial Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM). The PBM grants preferred formulary status in exchange for contracted rebates off list price. Meanwhile, the patient uses an AbbVie copay card to cap out-of-pocket costs.

web_blocks.title: Neuroscience ($10.8B in FY25): Psychiatry, Migraine, and Parkinson's

web_blocks.html: Neuroscience is AbbVie's second-largest and fastest-growing major pillar. Sales grew +19.6% in FY2025 and +21.6% in 9M 2026 [2, 3]. The unit spans Botox Therapeutic (chronic migraine, spasticity, cervical dystonia) and Vraylar (bipolar I and adjunctive major depression). It also includes oral CGRP drugs Ubrelvy (acute migraine) and Qulipta (preventive migraine), plus Parkinson's drugs Vyalev and newly approved Juvmo (tavapadon) [3, 7]. In a real-world migraine case, a 41-year-old office worker with 16 headache days per month visits a neurologist. Commercial insurers require patients to try generic beta-blockers and topiramate first. After those fail, the neurologist prescribes Qulipta (a daily oral CGRP blocker) for prevention and Ubrelvy as an acute rescue pill. Prescriptions route through retail or mail-order pharmacies under Medicare Part D or commercial plans. AbbVie supports access with prior-authorization help and copay cards. For a 68-year-old with advanced Parkinson's and severe motor swings, a specialist prescribes Vyalev. This 24-hour subcutaneous pump delivers foslevodopa/foscarbidopa continuously, avoiding the invasive intestinal tube surgery required by older Duodopa [3]. Together, these therapies make Neuroscience a durable multi-billion-dollar growth engine alongside Immunology [2, 3].

web_blocks.title: Oncology ($6.7B in FY25): Navigating the Transition from Imbruvica to ADCs and Bispecifics

web_blocks.html: Oncology is a portfolio in transition. Legacy BTK inhibitor Imbruvica (co-marketed with Johnson & Johnson) fell 14.3% in FY2025 to $2.87B and 26.8% in 9M 2026 to $1.61B [2, 3]. That drop reflects second-generation BTK rivals (Calquence, Brukinsa) and the January 2026 Medicare IRA price of $9,319 per 30-day supply [17]. Three newer drugs offset that drag: BCL-2 inhibitor Venclexta ($2.79B in FY25, +8.1%), ovarian cancer ADC Elahere ($690M in FY25, +44.0%), and CD3xCD20 bispecific Epkinly ($271M in FY25, +85.5%, partnered with Genmab) [2, 3]. In a real-world oncology case, a 64-year-old woman has platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Her tumor tests positive for folate receptor-alpha (FRα) via a companion diagnostic assay. A gynecologic oncologist treats her at a hospital outpatient infusion center. The clinic buys Elahere directly from a specialty distributor under the 'buy-and-bill' medical benefit (Medicare Part B or commercial medical coverage). Staff infuse the drug every three weeks and bill the payer for both the medicine and the infusion. That hospital model differs sharply from pharmacy-dispensed oral pills.

web_blocks.title: Aesthetics ($4.9B) and Eye Care & Other ($5.8B): Cash-Pay Consumer vs. Specialty Rx

web_blocks.html: Allergan Aesthetics runs on a very different economic model from the rest of AbbVie. It is largely cash-pay, insulated from PBMs and Medicare IRA rebates, but tied to consumer discretionary spending [3, 7]. In a real-world case, a 45-year-old consumer books a visit at a suburban dermatology clinic or medspa for forehead lines and cheek volume loss. The clinic buys Botox Cosmetic vials and Juvederm Voluma syringes directly from Allergan Aesthetics. Clinics earn volume tier discounts and bundle rewards through AbbVie's Allē consumer loyalty app. The patient pays out of pocket ($400 to $1,500+ per visit) with zero insurance involved. Botox Cosmetic rebounded +9.5% in 9M 2026, while Juvederm fillers fell 15.6% in FY2025 and 6.0% in 9M 2026 amid consumer caution and Galderma competition [2, 3]. Eye Care ($2.11B in FY25) supplies glaucoma drops (Lumigan/Ganfort) and retinal implants (Ozurdex) to eye doctors. Other Key Products ($3.74B in FY25) includes Creon ($1.51B, pancreatic enzymes), Mavyret ($1.32B, Hepatitis C cure), and Linzess ($907M, IBS-C, co-marketed with Ironwood) [2]. Linzess faces a Medicare IRA price cut to $136/month in 2027 [18]. Together, these five pillars give AbbVie wide reach across biologics, psychiatry, oncology, and cash-pay aesthetics. Still, nearly half of total sales remain concentrated in just two immunology brands.

web_blocks.title: Revenue Mix Concentration Check
paragraphs: Skyrizi and Rinvoq combined for $25.87B (42.3% of total sales) in FY2025 and $23.11B (46.8% of total sales) in 9M 2026 [2, 3]. AbbVie successfully replaced Humira, yet it recreated a two-product concentration in Immunology. U.S. patent durability through 2033–2037 and post-2030 pipeline execution are now the central structural questions. Without new pillars outside Immunology, any 2030s biosimilar shock would hit half of AbbVie's top line.

book_paragraphs: On paper, AbbVie's audited financial statements report one global pharmaceutical segment. That accounting rule reflects how the company shares manufacturing plants, clinical trial networks, and corporate overhead worldwide. To see how AbbVie earns its $61.16 billion in annual sales, we must look beneath that single line. Management runs five distinct commercial franchises: Immunology, Neuroscience, Oncology, Aesthetics, and Eye Care, plus a trio of legacy specialty drugs. Each franchise serves a different type of doctor, patient, and payer.

Nearly half of the entire business sits in Immunology. The unit generated $30.41 billion in 2025 and accelerated to $25.24 billion in the first nine months of 2026. A two-drug powerhouse drives the franchise: Skyrizi, an injectable IL-23 antibody, and Rinvoq, a once-daily oral JAK1 pill. Meanwhile, former flagship Humira shrinks steadily toward irrelevance. Together, Skyrizi and Rinvoq are pacing toward $32.1 billion in 2026 sales, roughly 50 percent above Humira's all-time peak. Picture a 34-year-old woman with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease who has stopped responding to older anti-TNF drugs. Her gastroenterologist prescribes Skyrizi. Following late-2026 FDA approval of subcutaneous induction, she no longer needs three clinic infusions. Instead, she starts and maintains treatment at home using an on-body injector every eight weeks. AbbVie ships the drug through a specialty pharmacy, which secures prior authorization from her PBM. AbbVie pays the PBM a contracted rebate off list price for preferred coverage, while a copay card caps her out-of-pocket bill. That home-delivery convenience helps Skyrizi hold half of new IBD patient starts.

Rinvoq plays an equally vital role on the oral side of Immunology. Consider a 48-year-old patient with severe ulcerative colitis or stubborn rheumatoid arthritis who prefers a daily pill over an injection. A specialist prescribes Rinvoq 15 milligram or 45 milligram tablets through the same specialty pharmacy network. Rinvoq already holds eight approved uses across rheumatology, dermatology, and gastroenterology, with vitiligo and alopecia areata filings pending in the U.S. That broad label gives AbbVie unmatched reach across autoimmune doctors. Even with a class-wide FDA boxed warning for JAK inhibitors, strong efficacy in bowel disease and eczema pushed Rinvoq past $8.3 billion in 2025 and toward $10.3 billion in 2026. Oral dosing keeps Rinvoq competitive with injectable biologics across multiple chronic conditions.

Neuroscience has quietly become AbbVie's second growth pillar. Sales hit $10.77 billion in 2025 (up 19.6 percent) and $9.49 billion in the first nine months of 2026 (up 21.6 percent). The unit blends three durable areas: therapeutic neurotoxins, psychiatry, and migraine and movement disorders. In migraine, a patient with 15 or more headache days a month usually tries older generic pills first. Once those fail, a neurologist prescribes Qulipta as a daily preventive pill and Ubrelvy as an acute rescue tablet. Both target the CGRP pathway. In psychiatry, Vraylar ($3.62 billion in 2025) treats bipolar I disorder and major depression through retail pharmacies. In Parkinson's disease, AbbVie's wearable pump therapy Vyalev is on pace to top $1 billion in 2026. Newly approved oral D1/D5 agonist Juvmo joins it to help patients control motor symptoms without raising oral levodopa doses. Those three legs give Neuroscience broad momentum across both office and retail settings.

book_subsections.title: Oncology: Bridging from Oral BTK Dominance to Solid-Tumor ADCs
paragraphs: Oncology is the one major franchise currently treading water. It generated $6.66 billion in 2025 and $4.98 billion in the first nine months of 2026. The drag comes from Imbruvica, the pioneering oral BTK pill for chronic lymphocytic leukemia shared with Johnson & Johnson. Under their deal, AbbVie books U.S. sales and shares overseas profits. Newer, cleaner BTK rivals and a 38 percent Medicare IRA price cut in January 2026 hit the brand hard. Imbruvica sales fell 26.8 percent in the first nine months of 2026 to $1.61 billion. That steep drop has masked steady gains across the rest of AbbVie's cancer portfolio.

To keep Oncology steady while Imbruvica fades, AbbVie leans on three newer drugs. Venclexta ($2.79 billion in 2025; $2.34 billion in 9M 2026) anchors fixed-duration leukemia regimens. Patients can stop therapy after twelve to twenty-four months instead of taking daily pills forever. Epkinly, a subcutaneous bispecific antibody partnered with Genmab, is growing fast in lymphoma. Most important, Elahere—acquired in the ImmunoGen deal—gives AbbVie a foothold in solid tumors. In practice, a woman with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer tests positive for folate receptor-alpha. She receives Elahere every three weeks at a hospital outpatient infusion center. Unlike pharmacy pills, Elahere runs on a buy-and-bill medical benefit model. The clinic buys the drug from a specialty distributor, infuses it, and bills Medicare Part B or a commercial plan for both the drug and service. Success in solid tumors will determine whether Oncology returns to double-digit growth.

book_subsections.title: Aesthetics and Eye Care: Cash-Pay Consumers vs. Legacy Cash Cows
paragraphs: Allergan Aesthetics ($4.86 billion in 2025; $3.64 billion in 9M 2026) operates in a completely different commercial world. When a consumer visits a dermatologist or medspa for Botox Cosmetic or Juvederm fillers, there is no insurer, no PBM rebate, and no Medicare negotiation. The clinic buys vials and syringes directly from AbbVie and tracks retention via the Allē loyalty app. The patient pays cash directly—often $400 to $1,500 or more per visit. That shield from government price controls is a real advantage. Still, it exposes Aesthetics to consumer caution. Juvederm fell 15.6 percent in 2025 and 6.0 percent in 9M 2026, even as Botox Cosmetic rebounded 9.5 percent. Aesthetic demand tracks household discretionary budgets far more closely than chronic autoimmune drugs.

Eye Care ($2.11 billion in 2025) and Other Key Products ($3.74 billion in 2025) round out the portfolio. In Eye Care, retina specialists inject AbbVie's Ozurdex implant ($493 million in 2025) for diabetic macular edema, while eye doctors prescribe Lumigan and Ganfort drops ($410 million) for glaucoma. Other Key Products includes Creon ($1.51 billion), a pancreatic enzyme taken with every meal by cystic fibrosis patients. It also includes Mavyret ($1.32 billion), an eight-week Hepatitis C cure, and Linzess ($907 million) for irritable bowel syndrome. Linzess, co-marketed with Ironwood, faces a steep Medicare price cut to $136 per month in 2027. Overall, AbbVie's portfolio is remarkably broad, yet its financial center of gravity is clear. Over two-thirds of the business now rests on Immunology and Neuroscience, making their distribution economics and manufacturing scale the next link to examine.

callouts.title: The Concentration Trade-Off
callouts.text: AbbVie solved its Humira problem by turning Skyrizi and Rinvoq into a $32 billion+ immunology duo. That success restored top-tier growth. However, nearly half of AbbVie's revenue now sits in two immunology molecules that will face their own 2030s patent cliffs.
